definition_zh: 首要的；主要的；最好的；上等的；青春；壮年；全盛时期；使做好准备；注水启动
definition_en: most important or of the best quality; the strongest period of a person's life; to prepare something in advance so that it is ready to work
core_image: 一排名字里被红圈标在最前面的那一个
scene: 董事会名单上，排在最前面的那个名字被圈了出来，旁边还写着一行小字：此事由他拍板。His prime task that morning was to count every crate in the store.
sceneCN: 这里 prime 是「首要的、最主要的」（第 1 个义项：最重要的）；句意为那天早上他的头等任务是清点店里的每一个木箱。图中可辨识物件：名单、红圈、批注小字。

pos.zh: 首要的；主要的；最好的；上等的
青春；壮年；全盛时期
使做好准备；预先交代；（给泵）注水启动

collocations.zh: 给泵注水；投入资金启动经济
让学生为考试做好准备

derivatives.zh: 由 prime 加 -er 构成，早期指「第一本书」，今指入门读物
由拉丁词干 prim- 加 -acy 构成，义为「首位；首要地位」
由拉丁语 primus 加 -al 构成，义为「最初的；原始的」
由 primary 加 -ly 构成，义为「主要地；首先」

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: more important than anything else in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在某一情形中比其余一切都重要
senses.example: Safety is the prime concern when the old bridge is repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 修这座旧桥时，安全是最要紧的事。
senses.why: The root simply means first, and the first item on a list of concerns is the one that outranks all the others.
senses.whyCN: 词根只表示「第一」，而在需要操心的一串事情里排第一，就是压过其余所有项的那一件，于是「第一」自然读成「最要紧」。

senses.title: Of the best quality
senses.definition: of the highest quality or in the best condition, as of meat, land or a position
senses.definitionCN: 质量最高、状态最好的，如肉、土地或位置
senses.example: The market sells prime beef from farms nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 这个市场卖的是附近农场出产的优质牛肉。
senses.why: What ranks first is also the pick of the lot, so the ranking word comes to describe the best cut or the best spot.
senses.whyCN: 排在第一的东西往往也是同类里被挑出来的那一个，于是这个表示次序的词又用来形容最好的一块肉、最好的一个位置。

senses.title: The best years of life
senses.definition: the period of life when a person is strongest and most capable
senses.definitionCN: 一个人体力与能力最强的那段人生时期
senses.example: He was in the prime of life when he took over the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他接手农场时正当壮年。
senses.why: A life also has a first and best stretch, so the word for what comes first was applied to the years before decline.
senses.whyCN: 人生也有最靠前、最好的那一段，于是表示「最先」的词被用来指衰退到来之前的那几年。

senses.title: To make ready in advance
senses.definition: to prepare a person, a machine or a pump beforehand so that it is ready to act
senses.definitionCN: 事先把人、机器或水泵准备妥当，使其随时可以运作
senses.example: The nurse primed the pump before the water could flow.
senses.exampleCN: 护士先给水泵注了水，水才流得出来。
senses.why: Priming a gun or a pump literally means filling it first, so the verb keeps the idea of putting something in before use.
senses.whyCN: 给枪装药、给泵注水，字面上都是「先填进去」，所以这个动词始终带着「使用之前先装好」的意思。

intro.en: Prime goes back to the Latin adjective for first, and each sense preserves that position in a queue: first in importance, best in quality, earliest in life, prepared beforehand.
intro.cn: prime 可追到拉丁语中表示「第一」的形容词，每个义项都保留着「排在最前」的位置感：最要紧、最好、人生最早的一段、事先备好。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written as *per- meant forward or before, and it is generally thought to lie behind the Latin word for first.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构形式写作 *per- 的词根表示「向前、在前面」，是拉丁语「第一」一词的更早来源。

items.en: Primus was the everyday Latin adjective for the first in order, rank or time.
items.cn: primus 是拉丁语中表示次序、等级或时间上「第一」的常用形容词。

items.en: The phrase prima hora, the first hour of daylight, gave a noun prima for the first hour of prayer, later felt as the early morning.
items.cn: prima hora 意为白天的第一个时辰，由此得到名词 prima，指第一个祈祷时辰，后来也被理解为清晨。

items.en: Old French used prim and its feminine prime for first, fine or delicate, and English borrowed the adjective in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语用 prim 及其阴性形式 prime 表示「第一的、精致的、纤细的」，英语在十四世纪借入了这个形容词。

items.en: Modern English uses prime for what ranks first, for the best years of life, and for the act of making a machine ready in advance.
items.cn: 现代英语用 prime 指排第一的事物、人生最好的岁月，以及让机器事先就绪的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin stem for first; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what outranks the rest.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「第一」词干上的词；近义组收表示压过其余者的形容词。

entries.definition: First in order or importance; also the earlier stage of schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 次序或重要性上第一的；也指初等教育的。

entries.definition: A first book that introduces a subject to beginners.
entries.definitionCN: 向初学者介绍某学科的入门书。

entries.definition: Belonging to the earliest and simplest stage of something.
entries.definitionCN: 属于事物最早、最简单阶段的；原始的。

entries.definition: The position of being first or most important.
entries.definitionCN: 居于首位或最重要的地位。

entries.definition: Highest in rank or importance among a group.
entries.definitionCN: 在一群中等级或重要性最高的。

entries.definition: Largest or most important of several things.
entries.definitionCN: 若干事物中最大或最重要的。

entries.definition: Most advanced or most respected in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 在某领域最前列或最受敬重的。

entries.definition: Best possible under the given conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 在既定条件下最好的；最优的。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on the single Latin adjective for first, and its senses measure that position in lists, in quality, in a lifetime and in preparation.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词只依托拉丁语中「第一」这一个形容词，各义项分别把这一位置放到名单、品质、一生和准备工作里去衡量。

normal.en: Primus is Latin for first, so prime always carries a ranking: first in importance, first in quality, first years of life.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 primus 意为第一，所以 prime 始终带着排序：最要紧、最好、人生最初的那几年。

normal.en: A prime minister is the first minister, the one ranked above the rest of the cabinet.
normal.cn: prime minister 字面是「第一位大臣」，即排在其余内阁成员之前的那位。

normal.en: Prime time is the first-choice slot of the evening, when the largest audience is watching.
normal.cn: prime time 是晚间最被看重的时段，收看的人最多。

normal.en: To prime a pump is to pour water in first, before the pump can draw anything up.
normal.cn: 给泵注水，就是在泵能抽水之前先把水灌进去。

normal.en: Prince is built from the same primus plus capere, to take: a prince is the one who takes first place.
normal.cn: prince 也由同一个 primus 加 capere（取）构成，原意是「占取第一位的人」。

abstract.en: Picture a queue: prime is the person standing at the very front, and everyone else is measured from that spot.
abstract.cn: 想象一列队伍：prime 就是站在最前面的那个人，其余人都以这个位置为参照。

abstract.en: The same front position becomes the first hour of a day, the strongest years of a life, and the water poured in before a pump starts.
abstract.cn: 同一个「最前」的位置，可以变成一天里的第一个时辰、一生中最强的那几年，以及泵启动前先灌进去的水。

abstract.en: Anything primed has been filled in advance, so the word ties being early to being ready.
abstract.cn: 凡是 primed 的东西都是提前装好的，所以这个词把「早」和「就绪」绑在了一起。

examples.en: The prime cause of the fire was a faulty wire.
examples.cn: 这场火灾的首要起因是一根故障电线。

examples.en: She bought a piece of prime land near the river.
examples.cn: 她在河边买了一块上好的地。

examples.en: He is past his prime but still plays well.
examples.cn: 他已过了巅峰期，但球还打得不错。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普赖姆」——谐音像「扑来第一」，扑过去抢到最前面，所以 prime 是首要的、第一的。

root: 拉丁语 primus（第一、最前）经古法语进入英语；同族词多与「第一、最初」有关。prime 与 prince 都出自 primus，但 prince 的后半截来自 capere（取），原意是「占第一位的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is first place; from that position the senses spread to the best quality, the strongest years of life, and the act of loading something in advance.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「排第一的位置」；义项由此分到最好的品质、人生最强的岁月，以及事先把东西装进去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one name circled at the very top of a list.
core.cn: 核心意象：名单最上方被圈出的那一个名字。

branches.en: the first name on a list of worries
branches.cn: 一列操心之事里排第一的那个名字

branches.en: a captain putting the crew above the schedule
branches.cn: 船长把船员安全放在进度之前

branches.en: the best cut of beef on the butcher's block
branches.cn: 肉案上最好的一块牛肉

branches.en: a farmer in his strongest years taking over the land
branches.cn: 正当壮年的农夫接手田地

branches.en: water poured into a pump before it can draw
branches.cn: 水泵先注水才能抽水

intro.en: A Latin adjective for first, plus a handful of English endings that turn it into a noun, an adverb and a beginner's book.
intro.cn: 一个表示「第一」的拉丁形容词，再加几个英语词尾，就变出了名词、副词和入门书。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus, first, also produced primarius, of the first rank, and the family reached English through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primus（第一）还派生出 primarius（第一等的），这一族词经古法语进入英语。

items.meaningCN: 次序或重要性上第一的

definition_zh: 原始的；早期的；简陋的；基本的
definition_en: belonging to an early stage of development; simple or basic rather than advanced
core_image: 一根削尖的树枝与一块打制的石片，旁边摆着一台精密仪器，两者对照出「最初的样子」
scene: 展柜里，削尖的树枝与打制石片被标为最初阶段，旁边是一台精密仪器。A primitive toolkit of sharpened sticks and knapped stone lay beside a precision instrument.
sceneCN: 这里 primitive 指「属于最早阶段的、未加工的」（第 1 个义项：原始的、早期的）；句意为展柜里一套削尖树枝与打制石片的原始工具放在精密仪器旁边。可辨识物件：树枝、石片、展柜、仪器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 原始的；早期的；简陋的；基本的；原始派的
原始派画家；原初事物

derivatives.zh: primitive（原始的）+ -ly（古英语 -līce，方式副词）→ 原始地；简陋地
primitive（原始的）+ -ness（古英语 -nes，性质名词）→ 原始性；简陋
primitive（原始的）+ -ism（拉丁 -ismus，主义）→ 原始主义
primitive（原始的）+ art（艺术）→ 原始派艺术
primitive（原始的）+ -ist（主义者）→ 原始主义者

senses.title: Belonging to the earliest stage
senses.definition: belonging to an early stage of development, before refinement
senses.definitionCN: 属于发展的早期阶段，尚未精细化
senses.example: Primitive tools were made by striking one stone against another.
senses.exampleCN: 原始工具是把一块石头往另一块上打制而成的。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin primus 'first', so its core sense is simply 'of the first stage'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由拉丁 primus「第一」构成，核心义就是「属于第一阶段」。

senses.title: Simple and rough
senses.definition: simple to the point of being uncomfortable or inadequate
senses.definitionCN: 简单到令人不适或不够用的程度
senses.example: The camp had only primitive washing facilities.
senses.exampleCN: 营地只有极为简陋的洗浴设施。
senses.why: Because early stages lack refinement, 'first' easily slides into 'rough' when applied to living conditions.
senses.whyCN: 由于早期阶段缺少打磨，「第一」用于生活条件时很容易滑向「粗糙」。

senses.title: A dated word for peoples
senses.titleCN: 未开化的（旧用法，含贬义）
senses.definition: an old and now discredited label for peoples considered less advanced
senses.definitionCN: 旧时对被视为不发达民族的一种标签，如今已被否定且含贬义
senses.example: Nineteenth-century writers used primitive in ways that modern anthropology rejects.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪作者使用 primitive 的方式，现代人类学已予否定。
senses.why: The label assumed a single ladder of progress, and the word inherited that assumption.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签预设了一条单一的进步阶梯，词义也继承了这一预设。

senses.title: Undeveloped in biology
senses.definition: in an early or undifferentiated form, as a cell or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 处于早期或未分化状态，如细胞或组织
senses.example: The embryo's primitive streak marks the first axis of the body.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎的原条标出身体的第一条轴线。
senses.why: Biology uses 'first-stage' literally: the structure appears before its later specializations.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把「第一阶段」用得很实：该结构出现在后来的特化之前。

senses.title: Taken as basic in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑与数学中的初始的
senses.definition: accepted without definition, as a starting notion in a system
senses.definitionCN: 在系统中作为起点而不加定义地接受
senses.example: Point and line are primitive notions in that geometry.
senses.exampleCN: 在那套几何里，点与线是初始概念。
senses.why: A primitive notion is one you cannot derive, so the word keeps its 'first' sense exactly.
senses.whyCN: 初始概念是无法推导的东西，因此这个词精确保留了「第一」义。

senses.title: Art outside the academic tradition
senses.definition: art by self-taught makers or from traditions outside formal training
senses.definitionCN: 自学作者或学院传统之外的艺术
senses.example: The exhibition placed primitive art beside trained portraiture.
senses.exampleCN: 展览把原始派艺术与受过训练的人像画并置。
senses.why: Collectors used the word for work they saw as untrained, and the label survived in art history.
senses.whyCN: 收藏家用这个词指他们眼中未受训练的作品，这个标签在艺术史中保留下来。

senses.title: A self-taught painter's style
senses.definition: a style marked by flat perspective and strong outline
senses.definitionCN: 以平面透视与强烈轮廓为特征的风格
senses.example: The primitive painter filled the canvas with flat houses and bright roofs.
senses.exampleCN: 这位自学画家在画布上排满平面房屋和鲜艳屋顶。
senses.why: The style sense comes from the makers rather than the period, so a modern untrained painter can still be called primitive.
senses.whyCN: 风格义来自作者而非年代，因此现代的自学画家仍可被称为原始派。

senses.title: A root word in linguistics
senses.definition: a word that is not derived from another word in the same language
senses.definitionCN: 在同一语言中不由别的词派生的词
senses.example: Hand is a primitive word, while handful is derived.
senses.exampleCN: 「手」是词根词，而由它加后缀构成的「一把之量」是派生词。
senses.why: Linguistics borrows the 'first' sense: the word stands at the base of a derivational family.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了「第一」义：这个词位于一个派生词族的基底。

intro.en: Primitive comes from Latin primus 'first' through the derived adjective primitivus and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: primitive 来自拉丁 primus「第一」，经派生形容词 primitivus 与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Primus meant 'first'; it also gives prime, primary, primate and primal, so the family is large.
items.cn: primus 意为「第一」，也产生 prime、primary、primate 与 primal，因此词族很大。

items.en: Primitivus meant 'first of its kind, earliest', built from primus plus the adjective ending -ivus.
items.cn: primitivus 意为「同类中最早的」，由 primus 加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。

items.en: Old French primitif carried the adjective into English in the fifteenth century, first in religious language.
items.cn: 古法语 primitif 在 15 世纪把这个形容词带入英语，最初用于宗教语言。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was used for art outside academic training and for peoples judged less advanced, a use now rejected.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，这个词被用于学院训练之外的艺术，也被用于被判定为不发达的民族，后者如今已被否定。

items.en: Biology and logic kept the literal 'first' sense: a primitive structure or notion is one that comes before the rest.
items.cn: 生物学与逻辑学保留了字面的「第一」义：初始结构或初始概念都先于其余部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the Indo-European root behind primus is reconstructed as per 'forward, before', a reconstruction and not a recorded form; the fifteenth-century English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：primus 之前的印欧词根被重构为 per「向前、在前」，属重构形式而非有记录的形式；英语 15 世纪的首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin 'first' root with different ranks; group two holds near meanings that describe stage or finish.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「第一」词根、但等级不同的词；第二组是描述阶段或完成度的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin primus 'first'; it means first in importance or the best period, not earliest in time.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primus「第一」；指地位首要或全盛期，而非时间上最早。

entries.definition: From Latin primarius 'of the first rank'; it means first in order or basic.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primarius「居首的」；指次序第一或基础性的。

entries.definition: From Latin primas 'of the first rank'; the animal order was named as the 'first' order by Linnaeus.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primas「居首位的」；动物目名是林奈把它列为「第一」目而来。

entries.definition: From primus plus -al; it stresses what is earliest and most instinctive.
entries.definitionCN: 由 primus 加 -al 构成；强调最早、最本能的部分。

entries.definition: Simply first in time, with no judgment about refinement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指时间上早，不含精细程度的判断。

entries.definition: Rough and unrefined, often implying poor workmanship rather than an early stage.
entries.definitionCN: 粗糙未加工，常指做工差，而非发展阶段早。

entries.definition: Serving as a foundation, with no suggestion of being outdated.
entries.definitionCN: 作为基础的，不含过时之意。

entries.definition: Not yet grown or elaborated, used of land, ideas or organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未成长或展开，用于土地、想法或生物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real primus family and the scientific senses that keep 'first' literally.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 primus 词族，以及保留字面「第一」的科学义项。

normal.en: Latin primus 'first' gives prime, primary, primate and primal.
normal.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」产生 prime、primary、primate 与 primal。

normal.en: The comparative is more primitive, not primitiver.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more primitive，不写作 primitiver。

normal.en: Biology keeps 'first' literally in primitive streak and primitive cell.
normal.cn: 生物学在「原条」「原初细胞」中保留字面的「第一」。

normal.en: Logic uses primitive notion for a starting idea taken without definition.
normal.cn: 逻辑学用 primitive notion 指不加定义的初始概念。

normal.en: The anthropological label is now avoided in careful writing.
normal.cn: 人类学的旧标签如今在严谨写作中已被避免。

abstract.en: Picture a sharpened stick lying beside a polished instrument.
abstract.cn: 想象一根削尖的树枝躺在一台光亮的仪器旁。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing with a flat sky and a bright roof, made by someone who never trained.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅天空扁平的画，屋顶鲜亮，出自从未受过训练的人之手。

abstract.en: Picture a first step on a staircase whose top you cannot yet see.
abstract.cn: 想象楼梯的第一级，顶端还看不见。

examples.en: The primitive plough was no more than a pointed branch.
examples.cn: 原始犁不过是一根削尖的树枝。

examples.en: The village had primitive drainage and no running water.
examples.cn: 这个村子排水简陋，也没有自来水。

examples.en: Point and line are primitive notions in the system.
examples.cn: 点与线在该系统中是初始概念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pri（第一）＋mitive」——排在第一、最早的样子 → 原始的

root: 拉丁 primus「第一」+ 形容词词尾 -ivus 构成 primitivus「同类中最早的」，经古法语 primitif 入英语；primus 之前的印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the literal first stage, then move to rough conditions, the discredited label for peoples, undifferentiated biology, logic that takes its starting notions without definition, art outside training, a self-taught style and a root word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面的第一阶段出发，随后是简陋条件、已被否定的民族标签、未分化的生物结构、不加定义的逻辑起点、学院外的艺术、自学画风与词根词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharpened stick beside a precision instrument, the first step before the polished one.
core.cn: 核心意象：削尖树枝与精密仪器并置，光洁之前的第一级台阶。

branches.en: FIRST STAGE: what comes earliest is also what lacks finish.
branches.cn: 第一阶段：最先出现的也往往最缺打磨。

branches.en: REJECTED LABEL: the old word for peoples rested on a false ladder.
branches.cn: 被否定的标签：旧时对民族的称法建立在虚假的阶梯上。

branches.en: LITERAL FIRST: biology and logic keep the sense of what comes before the rest.
branches.cn: 字面的第一：生物学与逻辑学保留「先于其余」之义。

branches.en: UNTAUGHT ART: makers outside training are named by their distance from the academy.
branches.cn: 未受训的艺术：学院之外的作者以其距离学院而得名。

branches.en: ROOT WORD: the base of a derivational family is 'first' again.
branches.cn: 词根词：派生词族的基底又回到了「第一」。

intro.en: Primitive belongs to the large Latin primus family, and its prefixes and suffixes show how 'first' branches into rank, time and foundation.
intro.cn: primitive 属于庞大的拉丁 primus 词族，其词缀显示「第一」如何分出等级、时间与基础三层。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus 'first' gives primitivus, primarius, primas and primal; the English endings -ly, -ness and -ism build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」产生 primitivus、primarius、primas 与 primal；英语后缀 -ly、-ness 与 -ism 构成其余部分。

items.example: Primus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: primus 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: The Latin adjective passed through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词经法语传来。

items.example: A primitive tool needs no finishing.
The primitiveness of the camp surprised them.
items.exampleCN: 营地的简陋让他们吃惊。
原始主义影响了早期现代绘画。

items.meaning: first in rank or the best period

items.example: The primate is our closest relative among mammals.
items.exampleCN: 灵长类是哺乳动物中与我们最近的亲属。

latinEntries.structure: primus, prima, primum (adj., first and second declension)
primitivus, primitiva, primitivum (adj., first and second declension)

primitive（原始的）+ -ness（古英语 -nes，性质名词）→ 原始性；简陋
primitive（原始的）+ -ism（拉丁 -ismus，主义）→ 原始主义
primitive（原始的）+ art（艺术）→ 原始派艺术
primitive（原始的）+ -ist（主义者）→ 原始主义者

definition_zh: 王子；亲王；君主；一方之主；（某领域的）巨子
definition_en: the son of a king or queen, or the male ruler of a small state; also a leading man in a particular activity
core_image: 披着斗篷的年轻人站在王座下一级台阶上
scene: 老国王病重，宫廷内侍捧着王冠站在长廊尽头，等着那位年轻的继承人前来。The young prince rode through the gate with his guard behind him.
sceneCN: 这里 prince 是「王子」（第 1 个义项：君主之子）；句意为年轻的王子在卫队随行下骑马穿过城门。图中可辨识物件：王冠、长廊、马与卫队。

pos.zh: 王子；亲王；君主；一方之主；巨子

collocations.zh: 童话中的白马王子；理想中的男子
威尔士亲王（英国王位继承人的称号）

derivatives.zh: 由 prince 加 -ly 构成，义为「王子的；如王子般慷慨的」
由 prince 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，义为「公主；王妃」
由拉丁语 princeps 的词干加 -ality 构成，义为「公国；侯国」

senses.title: The son of a monarch
senses.definition: a man or boy who is the son of a king or queen, or a close male member of a royal family
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王之子，或王室中关系亲近的男性成员
senses.example: The prince will take the throne when his mother steps down.
senses.exampleCN: 等母亲退位，这位王子将继承王位。
senses.why: Princeps named the man who took first place in the Roman state, and the title settled on the heir who stands first in line for the crown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 princeps 本指在罗马政权中占第一位的人，这个称号后来落到继承序列里排第一的继承人身上，于是有了「王子」。

senses.title: The ruler of a small state
senses.definition: a royal title held by the male ruler of a principality or by a noble of the highest rank
senses.definitionCN: 授予小国男性统治者或最高等级贵族的王室称号
senses.example: The prince ruled the mountain valley for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位亲王统治那个山谷四十年。
senses.why: Before it meant an heir, the word meant the man who actually held first place in a territory, so it still names the lords of small states.
senses.whyCN: 在指继承人之前，这个词先指真正在一方土地上占据首位的人，所以今天仍用来称呼小国之主。

senses.title: A leading figure in a field
senses.definition: a man who is outstanding in a particular art, trade or profession
senses.definitionCN: 在某一技艺、行业或职业中极为出众的男子
senses.example: He was hailed as the prince of pianists in his day.
senses.exampleCN: 在他那个年代，他被称为钢琴家中的泰斗。
senses.why: If first place can be held in a state, it can also be held in an art, so the title drifted from political rank to personal prestige.
senses.whyCN: 既然首位可以在一个国家里占据，也就能在一门技艺里占据，于是这个称号从政治等级滑向了个人声望。

intro.en: Prince descends from a Latin compound that joins first with take, so the word has always meant the man who occupies the front position.
intro.cn: prince 出自一个把「第一」和「取」合起来的拉丁语复合词，所以这个词一直指占据最前位置的那个人。

items.en: Primus, the Latin adjective for first, supplied the front half of the compound.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 primus 意为「第一」，为这个复合词提供了前半截。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize; in compounds it appears as -ceps, so the whole word pictures taking the first place.
items.cn: capere 意为「取、抓」，在复合词中写作 -ceps，整个词因此描绘出「占取第一位」的画面。

items.en: Princeps named the leading man of the Roman Senate and later the emperor himself.
items.cn: princeps 指罗马元老院中居首位的人，后来也指皇帝本人。

items.en: Old French prince narrowed the title to a ruler of high rank and to the son of a king.
items.cn: 古法语 prince 把这个称号收窄到高级统治者与国王之子。

items.en: English prince covers the monarch's son, the lord of a principality, and by extension a leading man in any field.
items.cn: 现代英语的 prince 既指君主之子、公国君主，也引申指任何领域中的领军人物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the prince family; the near-meaning group gathers titles for rulers and nobles.
note.cn: 形近组收 prince 这一词族；近义组收表示统治者与贵族的称号。

entries.definition: The female counterpart of a prince, by birth or by marriage.
entries.definitionCN: prince 的女性对应称号，因出生或婚姻而获得。

entries.definition: Belonging to a prince, or generous in the manner of one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于王子的；像王子般慷慨的。

entries.definition: A small state ruled by a prince.
entries.definitionCN: 由亲王统治的小国；公国。

entries.definition: First in rank or importance; also the head of a school.
entries.definitionCN: 等级或重要性第一的；也指校长。

entries.definition: A king, queen or other single ruler of a state.
entries.definitionCN: 国王、女王等一国之君。

entries.definition: A person who governs a country or region.
entries.definitionCN: 统治一个国家或地区的人。

entries.definition: A person of high social rank by birth.
entries.definitionCN: 出身高贵的贵族。

entries.definition: A noble of the highest rank below a prince in some systems.
entries.definitionCN: 某些制度中仅次于亲王的最高等级贵族。

normalIntro.en: The word joins the Latin adjective for first to the verb for taking, and the whole family keeps that picture of seizing the front place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语「第一」的形容词与「取」的动词拼在一起，整族词都保留着「占取最前位置」的画面。

normal.en: Princeps is primus plus capere: the one who takes the first place, which is why prince means both heir and ruler.
normal.cn: princeps 是 primus 加 capere，即「占取第一位的人」，所以 prince 既指继承人也指统治者。

normal.en: Prime and prince share the same opening, so both point at rank one; only the tail differs, and that tail is about taking.
normal.cn: prime 与 prince 开头相同，都指向第一位；区别只在后半截，而后半截讲的是「取」。

normal.en: Prince Charming is the prince of fairy tales, the man who arrives to close the story.
normal.cn: Prince Charming 是童话里的那位王子，故事靠他出场收尾。

normal.en: A crown prince is the heir standing closest to the throne.
normal.cn: crown prince 是离王位最近的那位继承人。

normal.en: The Prince of Wales is a title for the heir to the British throne, not a separate country.
normal.cn: the Prince of Wales 是英国王位继承人的称号，并不是另一个国家。

abstract.en: A prince is first place made visible: a person standing one step below a throne.
abstract.cn: 王子就是「第一位」的可见形态：一个人站在王座下一级台阶上。

abstract.en: Because the word is built from taking, it carries an edge that birth alone does not: the prince is the one who seizes the front.
abstract.cn: 由于这个词由「取」构成，它带着一种单靠出身得不到的锋利：王子是主动占住最前位置的人。

abstract.en: The same title slides from heir to ruler to master of an art, each of them first in their own circle.
abstract.cn: 同一个称号从继承人滑到统治者，再滑到技艺的宗师，每一个都在自己的圈子里排第一。

examples.en: The prince greeted the villagers from the steps of the palace.
examples.cn: 王子在宫殿台阶上向村民致意。

examples.en: The prince of that region signed a treaty with the neighbouring king.
examples.cn: 那一地区的亲王与邻国国王签订了条约。

examples.en: He was the prince of storytellers in that small town.
examples.cn: 在那座小镇上，他是说故事的人里的头一号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普林斯」——英文姓氏 Prince 音译作「普林斯」，记住这个词本来就是王子、亲王。

root: 拉丁语 princeps 由 primus（第一）加 capere（取）构成，经古法语 prince 进入英语；与 prime 同出 primus，但 prince 多出的 -ceps 表示「取」，所以本义是「占第一位的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the one who takes first place; the senses then spread from the heir of a crown to the ruler of a small state and to a leading man in any field.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「占第一位的人」；义项由此从王位继承人，分到小国之主，再到任何领域中的领军者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young man in a cloak standing one step below a throne.
core.cn: 核心意象：披斗篷的年轻人站在王座下一级台阶上。

branches.en: a young heir standing one step below the throne
branches.cn: 年轻的继承人站在王座下一级

branches.en: a crowd bowing as the heir rides through the gate
branches.cn: 继承人骑马穿门而过，人群躬身

branches.en: a mountain valley governed from a single castle
branches.cn: 一座城堡治理着整个山谷

branches.en: a title held by the lord of a small state
branches.cn: 一位小国之主持有的称号

branches.en: a pianist praised as first among his peers
branches.cn: 被赞为同辈第一的钢琴家

intro.en: The word is a Latin compound of first and take, shortened in French, and later fitted with English endings for the quality, the female form and the territory.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「第一」与「取」的复合词，在法语里缩短，后来再加上英语词尾，分别表示性质、女性形态与领地。

latinIntro.en: Latin princeps is built from primus, first, and the -ceps shape of capere, to take; the same primus also stands behind prime.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 princeps 由 primus（第一）与 capere（取）的复合形态 -ceps 构成；同一个 primus 也支撑着 prime。

definition_zh: 公主；王妃；亲王夫人；（口语）娇小姐
definition_en: the daughter of a king or queen, the wife of a prince, or a girl who expects to be treated like royalty
core_image: 长裙拖过石阶，女孩抬手扶住微微晃动的冠冕
scene: 舞会开始前，侍女替她理好裙摆，镜子里的女孩紧张得咬住了嘴唇。The princess stepped onto the balcony and the crowd below fell silent.
sceneCN: 这里 princess 是「公主」（第 1 个义项：君主之女）；句意为公主走上露台，下面的众人立刻安静下来。图中可辨识物件：裙摆、镜子、露台栏杆。

pos.zh: 公主；王妃；亲王夫人；（口语）娇小姐

collocations.zh: 王储妃；女性王位继承人
长公主（英国君主授予长女的称号）

derivatives.zh: 由 princess 加 -like 构成，义为「像公主一样的」
与 princess 同出 prince 一族，加 -ly 后义为「王子的；如王子般慷慨的」

senses.title: The daughter of a monarch
senses.definition: a girl or woman who is the daughter of a king or queen
senses.definitionCN: 国王或女王的女儿
senses.example: The princess learned to ride before she could read.
senses.exampleCN: 这位公主还没学会读书就先学会了骑马。
senses.why: Old French added the feminine ending to prince, so the word began as the female counterpart and settled on the monarch's daughter.
senses.whyCN: 古法语在 prince 后加上阴性词尾，这个词一开始就是 prince 的女性对应形式，后来固定指君主的女儿。

senses.title: The wife of a prince
senses.definition: the wife of a prince, or a woman who holds the title in her own right
senses.definitionCN: 王子的妻子，或以自身权利持有这一称号的女性
senses.example: The princess accompanied her husband to the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 王妃陪同丈夫出席了典礼。
senses.why: The feminine ending marked the woman attached to a titled man as well as a daughter, so marriage could also bring the title.
senses.whyCN: 阴性词尾既标记「有头衔者的女儿」，也标记「与他相配的女性」，所以婚姻同样能带来这个称号。

senses.title: A spoiled, demanding girl
senses.definition: a girl or woman who expects to be waited on as if she were royal and complains easily
senses.definitionCN: 期望被当作王室成员般伺候、动辄抱怨的女孩或女性
senses.example: Stop acting like a princess and help with the dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 别摆小姐架子了，来帮忙洗碗。
senses.why: A princess in stories is served by everyone, so the title became a mocking label for someone who demands the same without earning it.
senses.whyCN: 故事里的公主事事有人伺候，于是这个称号变成一种带嘲讽的叫法，指并未付出却要求同样待遇的人。

intro.en: Princess is the feminine of prince, made in Old French with a suffix borrowed from Greek, and it has kept both the honour and the mockery of a royal title.
intro.cn: princess 是 prince 的阴性形式，在古法语中用借自希腊语的词尾构成，至今同时保留着王室称号的尊崇与调侃两面。

items.en: Princeps, the compound of first and take, was the base that Old French turned into prince.
items.cn: 由「第一」与「取」合成的 princeps，是古法语造出 prince 的基础。

items.en: Late Latin used the feminine ending -issa, generally thought to come from Greek, for the wife or daughter of a title holder, as in abbatissa.
items.cn: 一般认为，晚期拉丁语用阴性词尾 -issa 表示有头衔者的妻子或女儿，这个词尾借自希腊语，例如 abbatissa（女修道院长）。

items.en: Old French formed princesse as the feminine of prince and used it for a prince's wife or daughter.
items.cn: 古法语造出 prince 的阴性形式 princesse，用来指亲王的妻子或女儿。

items.en: English borrowed princesse in the fourteenth century, spelled it in several ways, and kept it for women of royal rank.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 princesse，其间拼法不一，始终用来指王室女性成员。

items.en: Modern English puts the title before a name and, informally, uses it to tease a girl who expects to be served.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个称号放在名字之前，也在口语里用它打趣那些要求别人伺候的女孩。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the prince family and its feminine forms; the near-meaning group gathers female royal and noble titles.
note.cn: 形近组收 prince 词族及其阴性形式；近义组收女性王室与贵族称号。

entries.definition: The male counterpart, the son of a monarch or the ruler of a small state.
entries.definitionCN: 男性对应称号：君主之子或小国之主。

entries.definition: Belonging to a prince, or generous in the manner of one.
entries.definitionCN: 属于王子的；像王子般慷慨的。

entries.definition: A small state ruled by a prince.
entries.definitionCN: 由亲王统治的小国；公国。

entries.definition: A female monarch, or the wife of a king.
entries.definitionCN: 女君主，或国王的妻子。

entries.definition: The wife or widow of a duke, or a woman holding that rank.
entries.definitionCN: 公爵的妻子或遗孀，也指持有该爵位的女性。

entries.definition: A polite title for a woman of high rank.
entries.definitionCN: 对地位高的女性的尊称。

entries.definition: A king, queen or other single ruler of a state.
entries.definitionCN: 国王、女王等一国之君。

normalIntro.en: The word is the prince family plus a feminine ending, and that ending is the whole difference between the two titles.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 prince 词族加一个阴性词尾，这个结尾正是两个称号之间的全部差别。

normal.en: Prince plus the feminine -ess gives princess, exactly as actor plus -ess gave actress.
normal.cn: prince 加阴性词尾 -ess 得到 princess，正如 actor 加 -ess 得到 actress。

normal.en: Old French wrote it princesse, which is why the ending looks longer than a plain -ess.
normal.cn: 古法语写作 princesse，所以词尾看起来比单纯的 -ess 更长。

normal.en: A crown princess is either the heir to a throne or the wife of a crown prince, so context decides.
normal.cn: crown princess 既可指王位继承人，也可指王储的妻子，要看上下文。

normal.en: Princess Royal is a title a British monarch gives to his or her eldest daughter.
normal.cn: Princess Royal 是英国君主授予长女的称号。

normal.en: The mocking sense grows from fairy tales, where a princess never clears the table herself.
normal.cn: 那个嘲讽义从童话里长出来：故事里的公主从不自己收拾桌子。

abstract.en: The word is a title pinned on a woman by birth, by marriage, or by the way she expects to be treated.
abstract.cn: 这个词是贴在女性身上的称号，来由可以是出生、婚姻，也可以是她的行事做派。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps the idea of being waited on, which is why the same word can honour and tease.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留着「有人伺候」的意味，所以同一个词既能表示尊崇，也能用来打趣。

abstract.en: A suffix rather than a new root made the feminine form, so the core meaning of prince still sits inside it.
abstract.cn: 女性形式靠词尾而非新词根造出，所以 prince 的核心含义仍留在里面。

examples.en: The princess opened the new school in the village.
examples.cn: 公主为村里新落成的学校剪彩。

examples.en: She became a princess when she married the king's son.
examples.cn: 她嫁给国王的儿子后成了王妃。

examples.en: Do not be such a princess about the weather.
examples.cn: 别为天气这点事就摆小姐脾气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普林塞斯」——在「普林斯」后面添上「塞斯」，像给王子加上女字旁，就成了公主。

root: 古法语 princesse，是 prince 的阴性形式，词尾 -esse 源自晚期拉丁语 -issa（一般认为借自希腊语）；核心仍是 prince 那一族，只是换成了女性。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the female holder of a princely title; the senses spread from the monarch's daughter to a prince's wife and to a mocking label for a demanding girl.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是持有亲王称号的女性；义项从君主的女儿分到王子的妻子，再分到指娇纵女孩的调侃说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long skirt sweeping the stone steps as a girl steadies a small crown.
core.cn: 核心意象：长裙扫过石阶，女孩伸手扶稳一顶小冠冕。

branches.en: a girl learning to ride beside her father's guard
branches.cn: 女孩在父亲的卫队旁学骑马

branches.en: a young royal waving from a balcony
branches.cn: 年轻的王室成员在露台上挥手

definition_zh: 本金；主要的；校长；委托人
definition_en: the original sum of money borrowed; main or most important; a head teacher; one who authorises an agent

scene: 小李买房时向银行贷了一笔钱，还款表里第一项是本金，另一项是额外的费用。He paid off the principal of his mortgage ten years early.

senses.title: main or primary
senses.definition: first in importance or rank
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性或地位上居于首位的
senses.example: The principal cause of the fire was faulty wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾的主要原因是电线老化。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, direct from the Latin 'first, chief'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，直接来自拉丁语「第一、首要」。

senses.title: head of a school
senses.definition: the head teacher of a school
senses.definitionCN: 一所学校的校长
senses.example: The principal gave a speech at graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在毕业典礼上发表讲话。
senses.why: The head of an institution inherits the 'first, chief' sense.
senses.whyCN: 机构的负责人承接了「第一、首要」的意思。

senses.title: original sum lent
senses.definition: the amount of money originally borrowed, before interest is added
senses.definitionCN: 最初借来的金额，在加上利息之前
senses.example: Each monthly payment covers both principal and interest.
senses.exampleCN: 每月的还款既包括本金也包括利息。
senses.why: The original sum is the main part of the debt, separate from the interest that builds on it.
senses.whyCN: 原始金额是债务的主要部分，与在它之上累积的利息分开。

senses.title: party to a deal
senses.definition: a person for whom an agent acts in business or law
senses.definitionCN: 在商业或法律事务中由代理人代为行动的人
senses.example: As principal, she authorised her lawyer to sign the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 作为委托人，她授权律师代自己签合同。
senses.why: The one who authorises is the chief actor behind the agent.
senses.whyCN: 授权者是代理人背后的首要行为人。

senses.title: head of an embassy
senses.definition: the main diplomatic representative below an ambassador
senses.definitionCN: 低于大使级别的主要外交代表
senses.example: The embassy's principal met the foreign minister.
senses.exampleCN: 大使馆一等秘书拜会了外长。
senses.why: Another institutional 'first in rank' sense.
senses.whyCN: 另一种制度性的「首位」义。

senses.title: capital invested
senses.definition: money invested, as distinct from the income it produces
senses.definitionCN: 已投资的钱，与它产生的收益相区别
senses.example: The fund's principal remained intact through the downturn.
senses.exampleCN: 在衰退期间，基金的本金保持完好。
senses.why: The sum that sits underneath any return is the principal.
senses.whyCN: 任何收益之下的那笔钱就是 principal。

senses.title: main performer
senses.definition: the leading performer in a ballet, opera or similar
senses.definitionCN: 芭蕾、歌剧等中的主要演员
senses.example: The principal dancer fell ill before the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 主演在开演前病倒了。
senses.why: Again the 'chief, first' sense applied to cast ranking.
senses.whyCN: 又是「首要、第一」义应用到演员排序上。

senses.title: main road
senses.definition: a main road, especially in the town or the principal artery
senses.definitionCN: 一条主要道路，尤指城镇里的主干道
senses.example: The principal road was closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 那条主干道因维修封闭。
senses.why: A road that carries most traffic is the chief one.
senses.whyCN: 承载最多车流的路就是主干道。

intro.en: Principal and principle both descend from Latin princeps, but they split in meaning. Principal kept 'first in rank', principle took 'a rule'.
intro.cn: principal 与 principle 都来自拉丁语 princeps，但义分叉了。principal 保持「地位第一」，principle 则指「一条规则」。

items.en: Latin princeps meant 'first, chief'; it was built from primus 'first' + capere 'to take'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 princeps 意为「第一的、首要的」，由 primus「第一」+ capere「拿、取」构成。

items.en: Old French principal meant 'first' in the 12th century and passed into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 principal 在 12 世纪意为「第一的」，传入中古英语。

items.en: By the 14th century English principal meant 'chief person, head of a school', and by the 16th century the financial 'sum lent' appeared.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪英语 principal 已指「首要人物、校长」，到 16 世纪出现财务上「借出的金额」义。

items.en: Principle came through Latin principium 'beginning, rule'; it recorded the 'rule' sense that principal did not keep.
items.cn: principle 来自拉丁语 principium「起点、规则」，它承接了 principal 没有保持的「规则」义。

items.en: By the 19th century principal and interest became standard paired terms in loan documents.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，principal 与 interest 成为贷款文书里的固定配对术语。

items.en: Source solid: primus and capere are well documented. The split between principal and principle is a long-standing folk-etymology trap in English.
items.cn: 来源可靠：primus 与 capere 均有充分文献。principal 与 principle 的区分长期是英语使用者的陷阱。

note.en: Look-alikes are words with similar spelling; near meanings share the 'chief' or 'investment' territory.
note.cn: 形近是拼写相近的词；近义是与「首要」或「投资本金」领域邻近的词。

entries.definition: Money used to generate income; broader than principal, which is the amount of a debt.
entries.definitionCN: 用来产生收益的钱；比 principal 宽，principal 特指债务的金额。

entries.definition: A chief person; principal is more formal for the role.

entries.definition: A governing principle, but 'rule' is narrower than 'principle' (which is spelled -ple).

definition_zh: 原则；原理；准则；道义；（机器的）工作原理；本源（古义）
definition_en: a basic truth, rule, or belief that explains or guides how something works or how one should act
core_image: 一座建筑的承重柱：看不见整体，却撑着上面所有楼层
scene: 工程师向客户解释这台发动机。Fuel burns, the piston moves, and the crank turns: the same principle drives every model in the catalogue.
sceneCN: 这里 principle 是「原理」（第 3、4 个义项：解释事物如何运作的基本道理；系统工作原理）；句意：燃料燃烧、活塞运动、曲轴转动，同一个原理驱动目录里的每一种型号。图中可辨识物件：发动机剖面、活塞、曲轴、燃烧室、示意图；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A fundamental truth or rule
senses.definition: a basic rule or truth that other rules depend on
senses.definitionCN: 其他规则所依赖的基本规则或真理
senses.example: The course teaches the principles of economics.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授经济学原理。
senses.why: Latin principium means 'a beginning, a first part'. A principle is where a subject starts: the first thing you must accept before the rest can be built.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 principium 意为“开端、第一部分”。principle 是一门学科的起点：在其余部分建立之前，你必须先接受的那第一件事。

senses.title: A moral rule of conduct
senses.definition: a belief about right behavior that guides a person
senses.definitionCN: 指导人行为的关于正当行为的信念
senses.example: She refused on principle to lie.
senses.exampleCN: 她出于原则拒绝撒谎。
senses.why: Morality turns the architectural image into a personal one: a principle is a load-bearing belief. Break it and the rest of the person's conduct must be rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 道德把建筑意象变成个人意象：principle 是一根承重的信念。折断它，这个人其余的行为都得重建。

senses.title: A scientific law or mechanism
senses.definition: the basic way a natural process or device works
senses.definitionCN: 自然过程或装置运作的基本方式
senses.example: The principle behind the engine is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机背后的原理很简单。
senses.why: Science uses the word for the explanatory core: not a specific result but the rule that generates results. The principle is what remains true across cases.
senses.whyCN: 科学用这个词指解释的核心：不是某个具体结果，而是产生结果的规则。原理是在各种情形中都成立的东西。

senses.title: The working rule of a system
senses.definition: the rule by which a machine, method, or organization operates
senses.definitionCN: 机器、方法或组织运作所依的规则
senses.example: The pump works on the principle of expanding air.
senses.exampleCN: 这个泵依空气膨胀的原理工作。
senses.why: Engineering names the operating rule of an artifact. The principle explains why the design works, which is why it can be transferred to new machines.
senses.whyCN: 工程学给人工物的运作规则命名。原理解释设计为何有效，因此可以迁移到新机器上。

senses.title: A personal code of conduct
senses.definition: a set of values a person has decided to live by
senses.definitionCN: 一个人决定遵行的价值体系
senses.example: He is a man of principle.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一个有原则的人。
senses.why: When a person owns principles, the word becomes a character description. To have principles is to have a structure that does not bend with convenience.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人拥有 principles，这个词就成了一种品格描述。有原则，就是有一套不随便利弯曲的结构。

senses.title: Origin or source (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, the beginning or source from which something comes
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：事物由来的开端或源头
senses.example: Water was once held to be the principle of all things.
senses.exampleCN: 水曾被当作万物的本源。
senses.why: The oldest sense is 'beginning'. Greek philosophy asked for the arche, the first principle of things, and English used principle for that source before it narrowed to rules.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是“开端”。希腊哲学追问万物的 arche（第一原理），英语在收窄为“规则”之前，曾用 principle 指那个源头。

senses.title: In principle: as a theory
senses.definition: in the phrase in principle, as far as the basic idea is concerned
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in principle，就基本理念而言
senses.example: In principle the plan is sound.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上这个计划是合理的。
senses.why: The phrase separates theory from practice: the principle may hold even if the execution fails. It is a way of granting the idea without promising the result.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把理论与实行分开：即使执行失败，原理仍可成立。它是一种承认想法、却不承诺结果的说法。

senses.title: On principle: from conviction
senses.definition: in the phrase on principle, because of a moral or personal rule
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on principle，出于道德或个人规则
senses.example: He opposed the deal on principle.
senses.exampleCN: 他出于原则反对这笔交易。
senses.why: On principle marks a decision that is not pragmatic. The person is not weighing outcomes but obeying a rule, which is exactly what a principle is for.
senses.whyCN: on principle 标记一个非务实的选择。人不是在权衡结果，而是在服从规则——这正是原则的用途。

senses.title: A constituent element (archaic science)
senses.definition: in old chemistry and philosophy, a basic substance from which things are made
senses.definitionCN: 旧化学与哲学中构成事物的基本物质
senses.example: The four principles of the old chemistry were earth, water, air, and fire.
senses.exampleCN: 旧化学的四种要素是土、水、气、火。
senses.why: Before modern chemistry, 'principles' were the simple bodies into which matter could be resolved. The word then meant both beginning and ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 在现代化学之前，principles 是物质可被分解成的基本体。那时这个词兼指“开端”与“成分”。

intro.en: Principle comes from Latin principium, 'a beginning'. Its root princeps means 'first man', from primus 'first' plus capere 'to take'. The same root gives prince and principal, which is why principle and principal are so often confused.
intro.cn: principle 来自拉丁语 principium“开端”。其词根 princeps 意为“第一人”，由 primus“第一”加 capere“取”构成。同一个词根生成 prince 与 principal，所以 principle 与 principal 常被混淆。

items.en: First recorded as 'origin, source, fundamental truth', from Latin principium through Old French principe.
items.cn: 最早记录为“起源、源头、根本真理”，经古法语 principe 来自拉丁语 principium。

items.en: principium 'beginning, first part' comes from princeps 'first, chief', literally 'one who takes first place'.
items.cn: principium“开端、第一部分”来自 princeps“第一的、首要的”，字面为“占据第一位者”。

items.en: princeps = primus 'first' + capere 'to take, seize'. The chief is the one who takes the first place or the first share.
items.cn: princeps = primus“第一”+ capere“取、抓”。首领就是占据第一位或第一份的人。

items.en: principle comes from principium (a beginning, a rule); principal comes from principalis (first in rank). They share princeps but differ in meaning: a principle is a rule, a principal is a chief or a sum of money.
items.cn: principle 来自 principium（开端、规则）；principal 来自 principalis（等级第一）。它们共享 princeps，但含义不同：principle 是规则，principal 是首领或本金。

items.en: The moral sense 'a rule of right conduct' becomes common.
items.cn: 道德义“正当行为的规则”变得常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps principle for rules and truths, and principal for heads, main things, and sums of money.
items.cn: 现代英语用 principle 指规则与真理，用 principal 指校长、主要事物与本金。

note.en: The first group shares the princeps stem and the dangerous principle/principal pair; the second is about words that also mean a rule or truth.
note.cn: 第一组共享 princeps 词干与易混的 principle/principal 对，第二组看同样表示“规则”或“真理”的词。

entries.definition: chief; a school head; a sum of money. It comes from principalis, not principium.
entries.definitionCN: 主要的；校长；本金。它来自 principalis，而非 principium。

entries.definition: acting according to moral principles. It is principle plus -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 按道德原则行事的。它是 principle 加 -ed。

entries.definition: a royal ruler, from princeps 'first man'.
entries.definitionCN: 王子；亲王，来自 princeps“第一人”。

entries.definition: a statement about what must be done or what happens. It is broader and less foundational than principle.
entries.definitionCN: 关于必须做什么或会发生什么的陈述。它比 principle 更宽、更少基础性。

entries.definition: a binding rule, or a regular natural pattern. It is enforced or observed, not merely believed.
entries.definitionCN: 有约束力的规则，或自然规律。它被强制执行或被观察，而不只是被相信。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs taught by an authority. It is collective and official, unlike a personal principle.
entries.definitionCN: 权威所教的一套信念。它是集体、官方的，不同于个人原则。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin principium 'beginning', princeps = primus + capere, the principle/principal pair, and the phrases in principle and on principle.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 principium“开端”、princeps = primus + capere、principle 与 principal 这对词，以及 in principle / on principle 两个短语。

normal.en: Principium means 'beginning'. A principle is where a subject begins: the first thing you must accept.
normal.cn: principium 意为“开端”。principle 是一门学科的起点：你必须先接受的第一件事。

normal.en: Princeps is primus 'first' plus capere 'take': the chief is the one who takes first place.
normal.cn: princeps 是 primus“第一”加 capere“取”：首领就是占据第一位的人。

normal.en: Principle vs principal: a principle is a rule (from principium); a principal is a chief or a sum (from principalis).
normal.cn: principle 与 principal：principle 是规则（来自 principium）；principal 是首领或本金（来自 principalis）。

normal.en: In principle means 'in theory'; on principle means 'from conviction'. One is about ideas, the other about character.
normal.cn: in principle 意为“理论上”；on principle 意为“出于信念”。一个谈想法，一个谈品格。

normal.en: A person of principle is load-bearing: the beliefs hold up the rest of the conduct.
normal.cn: a person of principle 是承重的：这些信念撑起其余的行为。

abstract.en: A principle is a rule you keep when it costs you something; otherwise it is only a preference.
abstract.cn: 原则是付出代价时仍遵守的规则；否则它只是偏好。

abstract.en: Beginnings and rules are the same word because rules are where thought starts, not where it ends.
abstract.cn: 开端与规则是同一个词，因为规则是思想的起点，而非终点。

abstract.en: The principle/principal confusion is instructive: English once used one word for both a beginning and a chief, then split the labor.
abstract.cn: principle/principal 的混淆很有启发：英语曾用一个词兼指开端与首领，后来才分工。

examples.en: The machine works on a simple principle.
examples.cn: 这台机器依一个简单原理工作。

examples.en: She refused to sign on principle.
examples.cn: 她出于原则拒绝签署。

examples.en: In principle, the two systems should be compatible.
examples.cn: 理论上，这两个系统应当兼容。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑润色剖”——先把原则扑在纸上，再润色剖析 → principle 原则、原理

root: 拉丁语 principium“开端”，源出 princeps“第一人”= primus“第一”+ capere“取”。同根异义词：principal（主要的；校长；本金）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of principle, all versions of 'the first thing'. It can be the first truth of a subject, the first rule of a person, the first mechanism of a machine, or the first source of things.
sensesIntro.cn: principle 的九个义项都是“第一之物”的变体。它可以是学科的第一真理、个人的第一规则、机器的第一机制，或万物的第一源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load-bearing first rule that holds up everything built on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根承重的第一规则，撑起其上的一切。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: the basic truth explains how a subject or a natural process works.
branches.cn: 基础：基本真理解释一门学科或一个自然过程如何运作。

branches.en: CONDUCT: a moral rule becomes a personal code and a reason to act.
branches.cn: 行为：道德规则变成个人准则与行动理由。

branches.en: ORIGIN: the archaic sense names the source or constituent of things.
branches.cn: 本源：古义指事物的源头或构成要素。

branches.en: THEORY: in principle separates the idea from its execution.
branches.cn: 理论：in principle 把理念与执行分开。

branches.en: TRANSFER: an operating principle can be moved from one machine to another.
branches.cn: 迁移：工作原理可以从一台机器移到另一台。

intro.en: Principle is a noun from Latin principium. English adds -ed and the negative un-, and the princeps root also gives prince, principal, and principality.
intro.cn: principle 是来自拉丁 principium 的名词。英语加 -ed 与否定 un-，princeps 词根还生成 prince、principal、principality。

latinIntro.en: Latin principium 'beginning' and princeps 'first man' share primus 'first'. Principalis gives principal, while principium gives principle: same family, different jobs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 principium“开端”与 princeps“第一人”共享 primus“第一”。principalis 生成 principal，principium 生成 principle：同族不同职。

scene: 窗外雨声不停，车间里的机器一下一下压着纸，油墨味顺着门缝散出去。Every morning the shop would print the day's notices for the whole town.
sceneCN: 这里 print 是「印刷、印出」（第 1 个义项：把油墨压到纸上）；句意为这家店每天早上为全镇印当天的通告。图中可辨识物件：压纸的机器、油墨、门缝。

senses.title: To press ink onto paper
senses.definition: to produce words or pictures on paper by pressing an inked surface against it
senses.definitionCN: 用蘸了油墨的印版压向纸面，从而产生文字或图像
senses.example: The old press can print a thousand sheets in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这台老印刷机一小时能印一千张。
senses.why: The word comes from a verb meaning to press, so the action begins as pressure on an inked surface rather than as writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自表示「压」的动词，所以这个动作的起点是把蘸墨的表面压下去，而不是拿笔去写。

senses.title: To make a copy from a computer
senses.definition: to send a document from a computer to a machine that puts it on paper; also the paper copy so produced
senses.definitionCN: 把电脑里的文件送到机器上输出到纸上；也指这样得到的纸质件
senses.example: Could you print two copies of the report for the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 你能把报告打印两份带到会上吗？
senses.why: When computers entered the office, the same pressing action was handed to a printer, so the old verb was reused for the new machine.
senses.whyCN: 电脑进入办公室之后，同样的「压」交给打印机去完成，于是旧动词被直接借来指这台新机器干的事。

senses.title: A picture made from a plate
senses.definition: a picture produced by pressing an inked block, plate or screen onto paper, usually as one of a set
senses.definitionCN: 用蘸墨的木板、金属版或丝网压在纸上得到的图画，通常成套制作
senses.example: She hung a woodcut print above the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她在书桌上方挂了一幅木刻版画。
senses.why: Because the method repeats an image from a prepared surface, the noun names the picture that comes off the plate rather than the plate itself.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种方法是用准备好的版面反复复制图像，名词指的是从版上揭下来的那张画，而不是版本身。

senses.title: A mark left by pressure
senses.definition: a mark pressed into a surface by something touching it, such as a fingerprint or a footprint
senses.definitionCN: 某物接触表面时压出的痕迹，如指纹或脚印
senses.example: The police found a clear print on the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在玻璃上找到一枚清晰的指纹。
senses.why: Long before paper printing, the word meant the impression left by a stamp, and that older sense survives in fingerprints and footprints.
senses.whyCN: 在纸张印刷出现之前很久，这个词就指图章压出的痕迹，这个更早的意思活到了指纹、脚印这类说法里。

senses.title: To publish or carry in a paper
senses.definition: to include a piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine or book so that the public can read it
senses.definitionCN: 把一篇文字收进报纸、杂志或书里，让公众读到
senses.example: The paper decided to print her letter on the front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报社决定把她的来信登在头版。
senses.why: Publishing in the age of the press meant physically printing the text, so the machine's action became the word for making writing public.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷时代，发表文字就等于把文字真正印出来，于是机器的动作变成了「让文字公开」的说法。

intro.en: Print came into English as a noun for a pressed mark, from a French word for pressing, and only later grew the senses of printing text and pictures.
intro.cn: print 最初以名词身份进入英语，指压出来的痕迹，来自法语中表示「压」的词，后来才长出印文字、印图画的义项。

items.en: Premere meant to press or squeeze, and its participle pressus left marks on several European words.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」，它的分词 pressus 在多种欧洲语言里留下了痕迹。

items.en: Old French preindre, to press, formed the feminine past participle preinte, a thing pressed or stamped.
items.cn: 古法语动词 preindre 意为「压」，其阴性过去分词 preinte 指被压出、被盖上印记的东西。

items.en: The noun preinte named the impression itself, the mark that a seal or a block leaves behind.
items.cn: 名词 preinte 指印记本身，即印章或印版留下的那道痕迹。

items.en: Middle English took the word as print or prent, meaning a mark or stamp, and by the fifteenth century also a printed book.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 print 或 prent，指印记或图章，到十五世纪也指印出来的书。

items.en: With the printing press the verb spread to text and pictures, and in the computer age it was extended to paper output from a screen.
items.cn: 随着印刷机的普及，动词用法扩展到文字与图画；到了电脑时代，又扩展到屏幕上输出到纸面的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on print and its verb stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for making text or images public.
note.cn: 形近组收由 print 及其动词词干构成的词；近义组收表示让文字或图像公之于众的动词。

entries.definition: To make a copy of an image or text.
entries.definitionCN: 复制图像或文字。

normalIntro.en: The word began as the mark left by pressure and then moved to the machine that presses ink onto paper, so every sense is about transfer.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初指压力留下的痕迹，后来转指把油墨压到纸上的机器，所以每个义项讲的都是「转移」。

normal.en: Print comes from a verb for pressing, so the word still remembers the weight of a plate on paper.
normal.cn: print 出自表示「压」的动词，所以这个词至今记得印版压在纸上的分量。

normal.en: A printer is the thing that presses, and also the person whose trade was pressing.
normal.cn: printer 既是压印的机器，也是以压印为业的人。

normal.en: In print means the text has been pressed and is now public; out of print means the plates are no longer run.
normal.cn: in print 指文字已经印出、公开流传；out of print 指版子不再开印。

normal.en: Fine print is the small type at the bottom of a page, the part most people skip.
normal.cn: fine print 是页面底部的小字，多数人会跳过去不读。

normal.en: A fingerprint is literally a print made by a finger, the oldest sense still in daily use.
normal.cn: fingerprint 字面就是手指压出的印子，这是至今仍在日常使用的最古老义项。

abstract.en: Every sense of print is a transfer: ink to paper, screen to page, finger to glass.
abstract.cn: print 的每个义项都是一次转移：油墨到纸上，屏幕到纸面，手指到玻璃。

abstract.en: The word treats an image and a text alike, because both are pressed from one surface onto another.
abstract.cn: 这个词把图像和文字一视同仁，因为两者都是从一面压到另一面。

abstract.en: When a newspaper prints a letter, the physical act and the public act share one verb.
abstract.cn: 当报社 print 一封来信时，物理动作与公开行为共用一个动词。

examples.en: They print the school newspaper every Friday.
examples.cn: 他们每周五印校报。

examples.en: He printed the tickets and put them in an envelope.
examples.cn: 他把票打印出来放进信封。

examples.en: Her first novel is still in print after thirty years.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说三十年后仍在印行。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a mark made by pressure; from that the senses run to ink on paper, computer output, pictures from a plate, fingerprints and published text.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是压力留下的痕迹；义项由此通向纸上的油墨、电脑输出、版上揭下的画、指纹，以及公开的文字。

intro.cn: 一个表示「压」的拉丁动词、它在法语里的后裔，再加几个英语词尾，分别命名工人、机器与行业。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb premere, to press, has the participle pressus, which also lies behind the English word press.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 premere 意为「压」，其分词 pressus 也正是英语 press 的来源。

senses.title: A machine that prints text or images onto paper
senses.definition: a machine, usually connected to a computer, that puts text or pictures onto paper
senses.definitionCN: 通常与计算机相连、把文字或图像印到纸上的机器
senses.example: The printer ran out of paper halfway through the chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 印到这一章一半时，打印机没纸了。
senses.why: The ending -er marks the one that performs an action, and English has long let that ending cover tools as well as people, so the box that does the printing takes over the name of the hand that once did it.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 标记「执行动作的那一个」，而英语早就允许它同时指工具和人，所以这台替人完成印刷的盒子沿用了从前那只手的名字。

senses.title: A person whose trade is setting type and running a press
senses.definition: a worker who arranges type and operates a printing press
senses.definitionCN: 负责排字并操作印刷机的工人
senses.example: Her grandfather was a printer who could read type upside down.
senses.exampleCN: 她祖父是印刷工，能倒着读字模。
senses.why: Before machines, printing was work of the hands: one man set the letters, another pulled the bar, and whoever owned that skill was simply called the printer.
senses.whyCN: 在有机器之前，印刷全靠一双手：有人拣字，有人扳动杠杆，掌握这门手艺的人就被称作印刷工，这是最老的一层意思。

senses.title: A firm that produces printed matter
senses.definition: a business that prints books, newspapers or other material for clients
senses.definitionCN: 替客户印书、印报或印其他材料的商号
senses.example: The book was sent to a printer in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书被送到邻镇的印刷厂。
senses.why: Once the trade gathered into workshops with several presses, the same word moved from the craftsman to the business he ran, because a customer dealt with the shop and not with one pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 当这门手艺聚成拥有几台印刷机的作坊，同一个词就从手艺人转到他经营的商号，因为客户打交道的是那家店，而不是某一双手。

senses.title: A person who makes photographic prints
senses.definition: a person who produces final photographic prints from negatives or digital files
senses.definitionCN: 把底片或数字文件做成最终照片的人
senses.example: The printer adjusted the exposure before making the final copy.
senses.exampleCN: 冲印师在出最终成片前调整了曝光。
senses.why: Photography borrowed the word because a photographic print is also an image pressed onto treated paper, so whoever makes the final copy inherited the old title.
senses.whyCN: 摄影借用了这个词，因为照片同样是把影像压到处理过的纸上，于是负责做出最终成片的人继承了旧称呼。

intro.en: Printer is print plus an old agent ending, and print itself is usually traced through French to a Latin verb meaning to press, so the word starts from pressure rather than from ink.
intro.cn: printer 是 print 加一个古老的表人词尾；print 一般认为经法语上溯到表示「压」的拉丁语动词，所以这个词的起点是压力，而不是墨水。

items.en: The Latin verb premere meant to press, squeeze or push down, and its participle pressus stands behind the whole family of press words.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 premere 意为压、挤、按下，它的分词 pressus 支撑起 press 一族词。

items.en: Adding the prefix in- to premere produced imprimere, to press something into a surface, which is the picture behind every kind of printing.
items.cn: 在 premere 前加前缀 in- 得到 imprimere，意为把某物压进一个表面，这正是各种印刷背后的画面。

items.en: Old French used the noun preinte for an impression or a mark, and the verb preindre for making one; English took the noun first.
items.cn: 古法语用名词 preinte 指印痕、印记，动词 preindre 指压出印记；英语先借的是名词。

items.en: Middle English printen first meant to make a mark by pressure, and only later narrowed to pressing inked type onto paper.
items.cn: 中古英语 printen 最初指用压力留下痕迹，后来才缩小为把沾墨的字模压到纸上。

items.en: The agent ending -er first named the man at the press, and from the nineteenth century the same word was stretched to the machines that do the pressing for him.
items.cn: 表人的词尾 -er 先指站在印刷机旁的人；从十九世纪起，同一个词又被扩展到替他完成压印的机器上。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the print family and the Latin pressing stem; the near-meaning group gathers the other machines and trades that put marks on paper.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 print 词族与拉丁语表示「压」的词干展开；近义组收其他在纸上留下痕迹的机器与行当。

entries.definition: A machine that makes paper copies of documents.
entries.definitionCN: 把文件复制到纸上的机器。

entries.definition: A machine with keys that strike type onto paper.
entries.definitionCN: 用按键把字模打到纸上的机器。

entries.definition: A device that turns a printed page into a digital image, the opposite direction from a printer.
entries.definitionCN: 把纸页变成数字图像的设备，方向与打印机相反。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old agent ending laid on a verb that came from Latin pressing, so its reminders keep returning to pressure and to the hand that used to supply it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古老表人词尾加在一个源自拉丁语「压」的动词上，所以记忆线索总是回到压力和从前提供压力的那只手。

normal.en: Print comes from a Latin verb for pressing, so printing began as pressing rather than as writing.
normal.cn: print 出自拉丁语表示「压」的动词，所以印刷最初是压，而不是写。

normal.en: The -er in printer marks the one that does the action, the same ending as in teacher and builder.
normal.cn: printer 里的 -er 标记执行动作的那一个，和 teacher、builder 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: The machine sense is that same ending stretched to a tool, the way a computer is called a server.
normal.cn: 机器义只是把同一个词尾伸到工具身上，就像计算机被叫作 server 一样。

normal.en: Old French preinte gave English the noun print, and the t at the end is the trace of that borrowed participle.
normal.cn: 古法语 preinte 给英语送来了名词 print，词尾的 t 就是那个借来的分词留下的痕迹。

normal.en: Imprint keeps the Latin prefix in-: to press a mark into something.
normal.cn: imprint 保留了拉丁语前缀 in-，意思是把印记压进去。

abstract.en: A printer is a hand that became a box: the same job, the same pressure, only faster.
abstract.cn: 打印机是一只变成盒子的手：同样的活，同样的压力，只是更快。

abstract.en: Every printed page records two surfaces being pushed together, which is why the word belongs to the body before it belongs to the office.
abstract.cn: 每一页印刷品都记录着两个表面互相挤压，所以这个词先属于身体，后来才属于办公室。

abstract.en: When a word for a person turns into a word for a machine, a trade has been rebuilt around its tool.
abstract.cn: 当一个指人的词变成指机器的词，说明一门手艺已经围绕它的工具被重新搭建。

examples.en: The printer ran out of paper halfway through the chapter.
examples.cn: 印到这一章一半时，打印机没纸了。

examples.en: Her grandfather was a printer who could read type upside down.
examples.cn: 她祖父是印刷工，能倒着读字模。

examples.en: The book was sent to a printer in the next town.
examples.cn: 这本书被送到邻镇的印刷厂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普林特」——噗的一声，纸从机器里滑出来，那就是 printer。

root: print（印刷）加表人后缀 -er；print 经中古英语 printen、古法语 preinte 上溯到拉丁语 premere（压），加前缀 in- 的 imprimere 意为压印。

sensesIntro.en: The core is pressure transferring a mark; the senses divide into the machine that presses, the worker who once pressed, the firm that owns the presses, and the photographer who presses an image onto paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是压力把痕迹转移过去；义项由此分出压印的机器、从前动手的工人、拥有印刷机的商号，以及把影像压到纸上的冲印师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet sliding out of a machine, still warm from the ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸从机器里滑出来，还带着油墨的温热。

branches.en: a sheet sliding out of a humming box
branches.cn: 纸页从嗡响的机器里滑出

branches.en: ink-stained hands lifting a forme of type
branches.cn: 沾满油墨的手抬起字版

branches.en: a workshop with presses standing in the yard
branches.cn: 院子里摆着印刷机的作坊

branches.en: a darkroom tray holding a wet image
branches.cn: 暗房盘里浮着湿漉漉的影像

branches.en: the same pressure, once on paper and once on film
branches.cn: 同一种压力，一次压在纸上，一次压在胶片上

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing, its prefixed form, the French noun of an impression, the English verb, and the endings that name the doer and the trade.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示压的拉丁语动词、加前缀的形式、法语中表示印记的名词、英语动词，以及命名做者与行当的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere and its prefixed form imprimere stand at the head of this family, so the pressing image is recorded in Latin even though the modern trade word was shaped in French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 premere 及加前缀的 imprimere 处在这个词族的顶端，所以「压」的意象在拉丁语里就有记录，尽管现代行业词是在法语和英语里定型的。

a person or machine that prints

senses.title: Earlier in time
senses.definition: existing or happening before something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更早存在或发生
senses.example: She had prior experience in publishing.
senses.exampleCN: 她先前有出版经验。
senses.why: Latin prior is a comparative meaning 'former, first of two'. It compares two points on a line and names the one already passed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prior 是比较级，意为“前者、两者中的第一个”。它比较线上的两点，命名已经过去的那一点。

senses.title: Preceding in order
senses.definition: coming before in a series or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在系列或程序中出现得更早
senses.example: No changes may be made without prior approval.
senses.exampleCN: 未经事先批准不得改动。
senses.why: Procedures require gates: the prior step must be completed before the next begins. The word turns sequence into a condition.
senses.whyCN: 程序需要关口：前一步必须完成，下一步才能开始。这个词把次序变成条件。

senses.title: Higher in importance or rank
senses.definition: having a stronger claim or higher rank
senses.definitionCN: 拥有更强的请求权或更高的等级
senses.example: They have a prior claim on the land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这块土地有更优先的请求权。
senses.why: The Latin comparative could mean 'superior' as well as 'earlier'. Priority and precedence share the image of standing in front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁比较级既可指“更早”，也可指“更优越”。优先与居先共享“站在队伍前面”的意象。

senses.title: Before, in the phrase prior to
senses.definition: in formal usage, before a time or event
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：在某个时间或事件之前
senses.example: Prior to 2010, the firm had no overseas office.
senses.exampleCN: 2010 年之前，这家公司没有海外办事处。
senses.why: Prior to is the formal cousin of before. Legal and academic writing prefer it because it sounds procedural rather than conversational.
senses.whyCN: prior to 是 before 的正式表亲。法律与学术写作偏爱它，因为它听起来像程序而非口语。

senses.title: Presumed or existing earlier
senses.definition: in formal contexts, already held or existing before the present matter
senses.definitionCN: 正式语境中，在当前事项之前已持有或已存在
senses.example: The prior agreement still governs the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的协议仍管辖这场争议。
senses.why: Law speaks of prior agreements, prior art, and prior rights: things that existed first and therefore constrain what can be done now.
senses.whyCN: 法律谈 prior agreements、prior art、prior rights：先已存在的事物，因此约束当下能做什么。

senses.title: A monastic superior
senses.definition: the head of a priory or a religious house
senses.definitionCN: 小修道院或宗教院舍的首脑
senses.example: The prior welcomed the visitors at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 院长在门口迎接访客。
senses.why: The noun came into English in the 14c. from Medieval Latin prior, 'superior'. The monastic prior stands first in his house, the same rank image as the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词 14 世纪从中世纪拉丁语 prior“上级”进入英语。修道院院长在其院舍中居首，与形容词的等级意象相同。

senses.title: A previous conviction (informal)
senses.definition: in informal legal usage, an earlier criminal conviction
senses.definitionCN: 非正式法律用语：先前的刑事定罪
senses.example: The defendant has two priors.
senses.exampleCN: 被告有两项前科。
senses.why: Police and court slang clip the phrase 'prior conviction' to priors. The word's temporal sense becomes a record that follows a person.
senses.whyCN: 警察与法庭俚语把 prior conviction 缩略为 priors。这个词的时间义变成一份跟随此人的记录。

senses.title: The antecedent in logic
senses.definition: in logic, the proposition from which another is inferred
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中推出另一命题所依据的前一命题
senses.example: If the prior is false, the conclusion fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果前件为假，结论就不成立。
senses.why: Inference runs along a line: the prior proposition comes first and licenses the next. The temporal order becomes a relation of support.
senses.whyCN: 推理沿一条线运行：前件在先，并授权后件。时间次序变成支撑关系。

senses.title: Superior in rank (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, of higher rank or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：等级或尊严更高的
senses.example: the prior rank of a duke
senses.exampleCN: 公爵更高的等级
senses.why: This is the Latin comparative at full strength: prior as 'superior'. Modern English keeps the trace in the noun prior and in the idea of a prior claim.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁比较级的完整力量：prior 即“更优越”。现代英语在名词 prior 与“更优先的请求权”中留下痕迹。

intro.en: Prior entered English twice: first as a noun for a monastic superior, then as an adjective for 'earlier'. Both come from Latin prior, a comparative meaning 'former, first of two', which also gives priority and primacy.
intro.cn: prior 两次进入英语：先作名词指修道院院长，后作形容词指“更早”。两者都来自拉丁语 prior——一个意为“前者、两者中第一”的比较级，它也生成 priority 与 primacy。

items.en: The noun is first recorded for the superior of a priory or religious house, from Medieval Latin prior.
items.cn: 名词最早记录指小修道院或宗教院舍的上级，来自中世纪拉丁语 prior。

items.en: Latin prior 'former, previous, first of two' is a comparative of an old adjective *pri- 'before'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者、先前的、两者中第一”是古形容词 *pri-“在前”的比较级。

items.en: The root is traced to PIE *per- 'before, first', also behind first, prime, and principal. The reconstruction is standard.
items.cn: 词根被追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”，也见于 first、prime、principal。该重构是通行说法。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English with the sense 'earlier, previous'.
items.cn: 形容词在英语中记录为“更早的、先前的”。

items.en: prior to becomes a formal preposition, and the legal phrase prior claim spreads.
items.cn: prior to 成为正式介词，法律短语 prior claim 传播开来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious noun and the temporal adjective side by side, plus the informal plural priors for convictions.
items.cn: 现代英语让宗教名词与时间形容词并存，另有口语复数 priors 指前科。

note.en: The first group shares the prior/priority stem; the second is about words that also mean earlier or more important.
note.cn: 第一组共享 prior/priority 词干，第二组看同样表示“更早”或“更重要”的词。

entries.definition: the state of being first in rank or the thing ranked first. It comes from Medieval Latin prioritas.
entries.definitionCN: 优先地位；优先事项。来自中世纪拉丁语 prioritas。

entries.definition: a small monastery headed by a prior.
entries.definitionCN: 由院长主持的小修道院。

entries.definition: a female superior of a priory.
entries.definitionCN: 女修道院院长。

entries.definition: earlier, especially the one just before. It is less formal than prior.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的，尤指刚过去的那一个。它比 prior 少些正式。

entries.definition: the earlier of two, or a past role-holder. It contrasts with latter.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中在前的，或前任。与 latter 相对。

entries.definition: coming immediately before in order. It is purely positional.
entries.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接其前。它纯粹是位置性的。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prior as a comparative, the noun for a monastic superior, the phrase prior to, and the legal sense of a prior claim.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prior 的比较级性质、指修道院院长的名词、短语 prior to，以及 prior claim 的法律义。

normal.en: Prior is a Latin comparative: it compares two things and names the earlier one.
normal.cn: prior 是拉丁比较级：它比较两物，并命名更早的那一个。

normal.en: The same comparative can mean 'superior', which is why prior also means 'more important'.
normal.cn: 同一比较级也可指“更优越”，所以 prior 也表“更重要”。

normal.en: The noun prior is a different borrowing: the head of a priory stands first in his house.
normal.cn: 名词 prior 是另一次借入：小修道院院长在其院舍中居首。

normal.en: Prior to is formal 'before'; lawyers and academics prefer it to sound procedural.
normal.cn: prior to 是正式的 before；律师与学者偏爱它，以显得程序化。

normal.en: In police slang, priors are prior convictions: the past that follows a person.
normal.cn: 警察俚语中，priors 是前科：跟随一个人的过去。

abstract.en: Time and rank collapse into one word: what came first is assumed to deserve first place.
abstract.cn: 时间与等级在此塌缩成一个词：先来的，被假定该先得。

abstract.en: A prior claim is a promise the past makes to the present.
abstract.cn: 优先请求权是过去对当下作出的承诺。

abstract.en: The comparative form is the point: prior never stands alone, it always implies a second term.
abstract.cn: 重点在比较级形式：prior 从不孤立，它总隐含另一个项。

examples.en: You need prior approval before changing the budget.
examples.cn: 改动预算前需要事先批准。

examples.en: Prior to joining the firm, she taught at a university.
examples.cn: 加入这家公司之前，她在大学任教。

examples.en: The court considered his prior convictions.
examples.cn: 法庭考虑了他的前科。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来尔”——先扑过来排队的那一个 → prior 先前的、优先的

root: 拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”，是 *pri-“在前”的比较级；更早为原始印欧语 *per-。同族有 priority、prime、principal。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of prior, all comparative. The word always implies a second term: this one is earlier, or higher, or both. It can point to a time, a rank, a right, a monastic office, or a criminal record.
sensesIntro.cn: prior 的九个义项都是比较性的。这个词总隐含另一个项：这一个更早，或更高，或两者兼有。它可以指时间、等级、权利、修道职务或犯罪记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one standing earlier in the line, and therefore first in line.
core.cn: 核心意象：在队伍中站得更早、因而更靠前的那一个。

branches.en: TIME: an earlier point or step, including agreements already in force.
branches.cn: 时间：更早的时间点或步骤，包括已生效的协议。

branches.en: RANK: the comparative shades into superiority and precedence.
branches.cn: 等级：比较级滑向优越与居先。

branches.en: PREPOSITION: prior to is the formal 'before'.
branches.cn: 介词：prior to 是正式的“在……之前”。

branches.en: OFFICE: the monastic prior stands first in his house.
branches.cn: 职务：修道院院长在其院舍中居首。

branches.en: RECORD AND LOGIC: prior convictions, and the antecedent proposition.
branches.cn: 记录与逻辑：前科，以及逻辑前件。

intro.en: Prior is both adjective and noun. English adds -ity, -ize, and -y, and the Latin comparative also underlies priority and primacy.
intro.cn: prior 既是形容词也是名词。英语加 -ity、-ize、-y，拉丁比较级还支撑 priority 与 primacy。

latinIntro.en: Latin prior 'former, first of two' is a comparative beside primus 'first' and *pri- 'before'. Its noun prioritas gives English priority.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”是与 primus“第一”、*pri-“在前”相邻的比较级。其名词 prioritas 生成英语 priority。

items.meaning: to treat as more important than others
items.meaningCN: 优先处理（-ize 构成动词）

definition_zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序；（计算机）优先级
definition_en: the state of being more important than something else, or a thing that is ranked first
core_image: 急诊分诊台上，红色标签的伤员先被推进手术室
scene: 医院分诊时，护士把红黄绿标签贴在病历夹上。The triage nurse set the priority of each patient by colour, so the most serious cases were seen first.
sceneCN: 这里 priority 是「优先次序、优先级」（第 3 个义项：按重要性排出的先后顺序）；句意：分诊护士用颜色给每位病人排定优先次序，最危重的先看。图中可辨识物件：分诊台、红黄绿标签、担架、病历夹、时钟；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序
